calls.label: Why three wires
calls.says: Why are there three wires, and why does the black one matter?
calls.reply:
Two of the wires make the circuit actually work — the red brings power out to the sensor, and the black is the ground, the way back. Without the black one, current has no path home, so nothing flows at all, no matter what the red one's doing. The yellow one's the odd one out — that's just the sensor talking, telling the board what it's reading.

Right now though, you're still on laying everything out — have you got all eight parts sitting in a row where you can see them?

calls.label: What is an ohm
calls.says: What is an ohm, and why would I need a resistor?
calls.reply: An ohm is just the unit for how much a part resists electricity flowing through it — bigger number, less current gets through. A resistor uses that to protect something like a lamp from drawing too much current and burning out, but there's no resistor in this box, so it's not something you need to worry about yet. Right now you're on step 01 — have you got all eight parts laid out in a row?
